correctness.rationale: For an arbitrary maximizing sequence, countable support and finite-dimensional block compactness give a coordinatewise norm limit u. A recursive finite-block gliding hump gives pairwise disjoint b_j with ||Tx_nj-(u+b_j)||→0 and ||b_j||→1−||u||. For every ε choose one fε∈B_{Y*} norming the finite head of u and simultaneously all late disjoint b_j; it gives norm ≥||u||−2ε+1−||u|| for the same weak-star ultralimit T**ξ. The universal operator norm bound gives equality, forcing ||ξ||=1. Both real and complex scalars, uncountable Γ, nonzero/zero T and unbounded block dimensions are covered. A Hilbert diagonal shows the limit of the hypothesis. No numerical experiment substitutes for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Full relevant primary preprint sections and the nearest published third-adjoint record were inspected. The scalar ℓ1 case is already covered and is explicitly excluded from the novelty assertion. No inspected statement entails universal second-adjoint norm attainment into unrestricted ℓ1-sums of arbitrary finite-dimensional blocks. The gliding-hump argument uses coordinate compactness and accommodates unbounded, non-ℓ1 block geometry. An unindexed general disjointization result remains a genuine originality risk.
residual_risks: A broad unindexed structural theorem on L-embedded or norm-preserving weak-star subsequence limits could subsume the blockwise proof.

The extension from scalar ℓ1 to block ℓ1 uses the same general disjoint-support mechanism as the motivating work; novelty depends on the genuinely new target geometry, not on reinventing that mechanism.
Database retrieval is not a uniqueness proof; independent literature verification remains outstanding.

value.rationale: Adjoint-level norm attainment is a central recent geometric operator question. This establishes a universal-range theorem for arbitrarily heterogeneous finite-dimensional blocks, including the natural unbounded-dimension sequence (⊕ ℓ2^n)_{ℓ1}, with no restriction on source. The sharp structural boundary is meaningful: allowing a single infinite-dimensional Hilbert block admits a non-norm-attaining second adjoint. It is not an arbitrary example or a numeric gain. Explicitly credits the prior scalar ℓ1 subfamily; potential hidden L-embedded coverage is disclosed.
